content:
- Overestimate prices when sentiment is neutral or negative (no significant bullish signal), especially in early forecast windows.
- Underestimate prices after recent spikes if sentiment remains flat or slightly negative — model tends to overcorrect downward.
- Overshoot in the short-term (1-3 days) after a sharp price rise, then corrects — model overreacts to momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in the medium term (7-14 days) when sentiment is flat, then drops below true mean.
- When sentiment is positive (even low 0.00–0.33), model tends to overestimate 30-day horizon — especially if recent price is rising.
- If sentiment is negative (0.00) and price is trending up, model often fails to capture the upward momentum — underestimates.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging the true trend — especially if sentiment is flat or negative — model delays reaction.
- If sentiment is 0.00 and price is near recent peak, model often overestimates 30d — then underestimates in next period.
- Model tends to overestimate in the first 5-7 days of forecast horizon if sentiment is neutral — then corrects downward.
- If sentiment is 0.00 and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop — then overcorrects later.
